jŭvo, jūvi, jūtum, 1 (juvaturus, ; :
iuerint,), v. a. and n.
perh. root div-, to gleam; cf. dies
, to help, aid, assist, support, benefit (cf.: auxilior, subvenio, opitulor).
In gen.: qui se natos ad homines juvandos, tutandos, conservandos arbitrantur,: beatae vitae disciplinam juvare,: aliquem omni suo studio in petitione,: aliquem auxilio laboris,: hostes frumento,: juvit facundia causam,: imbres arva juvantes,: (Juppiter) juvat imbribus agros,: aliquem portuque locoque,by receiving into harbor and house,: nudum hospitio tectoque,: pectora alloquio,: audentes deus ipse juvat,: audentes Fortuna juvat,: aliquem in aliqua re,.—With two acc.: aliquid Rutulos,. —Of medical assistance: qui salutari juvat arte fessos,; ; : dis juvantibus or deo juvante, with God's help: me, dis juvantibus, ante brumam exspecta,; ; cf.: non denique quicquam aliud nisi juvantibus sacris deligunt,.—In pass.: lex Cornelia proscriptum juvari vetat,: viatico a me juvabitur,: precor, quaeras, qua sim tibi parte juvandus,: placuit sollertia, tempore etiam juta, (al. adjuta): nec sola (lingua) loquendi munus implere potest, nisi juta, etc.,.—Impers., juvat, it is of use; with a subject-clause: juvat Ismara Baccho Conserere,: quid docuisse juvabat?; cf.: quid juvat esse deum?.—
In partic., to delight, gratify, please: juvare in utroque (in sensu et in animo) dicitur: ex eoque jucundum,. —In this sense rarely as a personal verb: nec umquam quicquam me juvat quod edo domi; Foris ... quod gusto id beat,: non omnis arbusta juvant humilesque myricae,: nec me vita juvaret, invisa civibus et militibus meis,: si nec fabellae te juvant nec fabulae,: multos castra juvant,: aurem juvantia verba,.—In pass.: refer ad aures, probabunt: quaere, cur? ita se dicent juvari,.—More freq. impers., juvat (aliquem), with subject-clause, it delights, pleases, I (thou, he, etc.) am delighted, take pleasure in: juvit me, tibi tuas litteras profuisse,: juvat me haec praeclara nomina artificum ... concidisse,: forsan et haec olim meminisse juvabit,: juvat evasisse tot urbes Argolicas,: insano juvat indulgere labori,: si pereo, hominum manibus periisse juvabit,: quae scire magis juvat quam prodest,.

la:verb:iungo.gloss: to join, unite, fasten, yoke, harness, attach; esp. of the hand: to clasp, join
senses: to join, unite, fasten, yoke, harness, attach; esp. of the hand: to clasp, join
of a treaty or agreement: to join, unite, make; of marriage: to join, unite
la:verb:iungo.html:
jungo, nxi, nctum, 3, v. a.
Sanscr. jug, junagmi, to unite; juk, joined; Goth. juk; O. H. Germ. joh, joch; Gr. ζυγ, ζεύγνυμι, ζυγός, ζυγόν
,
to join or unite together, connect, attach, fasten, yoke, harness.
Lit.
In gen.
With acc.: Narcissum et florem anethi,: pontes et propugnacula,: nemoris carentia sensu robora,: gradus,to close the ranks,: montes,to heap up,: ostia,to shut,; cf.: junctas quatere fenestras,: oscula,to exchange,; cf. ; : da jungere dextram,to clasp,: cur dextrae jungere dextram non datur,; cf.: quas junximus hospitio dextras,; 11, 165: duos sinus,: juncto ponte milites transmittit,.—So with abl. of means or manner: Ticinum ponte,to span,: amnem ponte,: ratibus flumen,to bridge,; cf.: qui biduo vix locum rate jungendo flumini inventum tradunt,: eo omnia vallo et fossa,: plumbum nigrum albo,; cf.: nam calamus cera jungitur,: illos defendit numerus junctaeque umbone phalanges,: erga juncta est mihi foedere dextra,: Pompei acies junxerat in seriem nexis umbonibus arma,. —
With dat. of indir. object: hoc opus ad turrim hostium admovent, ut aedificio jungatur,: humano capiti cervicem equinam,: mortua corpora vivis,; cf.: his tignis contraria duo juncta,: se Romanis,: exercitum sibi,: socia arma Rutulis,: victores Germani juncturi se Pannoniis,: cervicem meam amplexui, dub. (Büch., vinxit amplexu): dextra dextrae jungitur,; cf. supra: aeri aes plumbo fit uti jungatur ab albo,: juncta est vena arteriis,: Comius incensum calcaribus equum jungit equo Quadrati,drives against,.—
With inter se: tigna bina inter se,: maxime autem corpora inter se juncta permanent, cum, etc.,: disparibus calamis inter se junctis,: saltus duo alti inter se juncti,.—
With cum: cum Bruto Cassioque vires suas,: legiones se cum Caesare juncturae,: erat cum pede pes junctus,: lecto mecum junctus in uno,: digitis medio cum pollice junctis,: lingua cum subjecta parte juncta est,.—
Esp.
To harness, yoke, attach.
Of animals: angues ingentes alites juncti jugo, Pac. ap. (Trag. v. 397 Rib.): junge pares,i. e. in pairs,; : nec jungere tauros norant,: currus et quatuor equos,: grypes equis, Forbig.: curru jungit Halaesus Equos,: leones ad currum,: mulis e proximo pistrino ad vehiculum junctis,.—
Of a vehicle (rare): reda equis juncta,: neve (mulier) juncto vehiculo veheretur,: juncta vehicula, pleraque onusta, mille admodum capiuntur,. —
Of wounds, etc., to join, bring together, unite, heal: ego vulnera doctum jungere Etiona petam,: parotidas suppuratas,: oras (tumoris),: oras vulneris,—
Of lands, territories, etc.: juncta pharetratis Sarmatis ora Getis,adjoining,; cf.: juncta Aquilonibus Arctos,: quibus (campis) junctae paludes erant,; : fundos Apuliae,to add, join to,: longos jungere fines agrorum,.—
To connect in time, cause to follow immediately: cum diei noctem pervigilem junxisset,: somnum morti,: vidit hic annus Ventidium consularem praetextam jungentem praetoriae,: nulla natio tam mature consino belli bellum junxit,: junge, puer, cyathos, atque enumerare labora,: laborem difficilius est repetere quam jungere,to resume than to continue,.—So of pronunciation: si jungas (opp. interpunctis quibusdam),.—
Milit. t. t., of troops, an army, etc., to join, unite: cum juncti essent,; : exercitum Pompei sibi,: junctis exercitious,: cum collegae se junxisset,; so, exercitum,: Ajacem naves suas Atheniensibus junxisse,.—
To add, give in addition: commoda praeterea jungentur multa caducis,.—
In mal. part.: corpora,: turpia corpora,: tu mihi juncta toro, ; : si jungitur ulla Ursidio,; ; cf. Venerem,; ; .
Transf.
In gen., of abstract things, to bring together, join, unite: cum hominibus nostris consuetudines, amicitias, res rationesque jungebat,: omnem naturam, quae non solitaria sit ... sed cum alio juncta atque conexa, etc.,: an virtus et voluptas inter se jungi copularique possint,: sapientiam junctam habere eloquentiae,: indignationem conquestioni,: insignis improbitas et scelere juncta,: plura crimina junguntur,are combined,.—
Esp.
Of persons, to join, unite, bring together, associate, in love, marriage, relationship, etc.: cum impari,: cum pare,: alicujus filiam secum matrimonio,: si tibi legitimis pactam junctamque tabellis non es amaturus,: juncta puella viro,; . —Of animals, etc.: Appulis jungentur capreae lupis,: variis albae junguntur columbac,: unaque nos sibi operā amicos junget,: ut quos certus amor junxit,: amicos,: Geminum mecum tua in me beneficia junxerunt,: puer puero junctus amicitia,.—Esp., of a treaty, alliance, etc.: si populus Romanus foedere jungeretur regi,; . —
Of things, to make by joining, enter into: pacem cum Aenea, deinde adfinitatem,: nova foedera,: cum Hispanis amicitiam,: societatem cum eo metu potentiae ejus,: foedus cum eo amicitiamque,; : juncta societas Hannibali,: foedera,: jungendae societatis gratia,.—
Of words, etc., to join, unite.
Esp., gram. t. t.: verba jungere, to make by joining, to compound: jungitur verbum ex corrupto et integro, ut malevolus,: in jungendo aut in derivando,; so, juncta verba,; .—
To connect so as to sound agreeably: quantum interest ... verba eadem qua compositione vel in textu jungantur vel in fine claudantur,.—Hence, P. a.: junc-tus, a, um, joined, united, connected, associated: in opere male juncto,.—Comp.: causa fuit propior et cum exitu junctior,.—Sup.: junctissimus illi comes,most attached,: principum prosperis et alii fruantur: adversae ad junctissimos pertineant,their nearest of kin,.

la:verb:iubeo.html:
jŭbĕo, jussi, jussum (jusso for jussero, ; :
justi for jussisti,.—Inf.: jusse,: jussitur for jubetur,), 2, v. a.
perh. = jus habere, to regard as right, hence
, to order one to do something, to bid, tell, command (syn.: mando, impero, praecipio).
In gen.: jubesne? jubeo, cogo atque impero,: ut justi (jussisti),: defessa jubendo, est saeva Jovis conjux,: sic jubeo, stat pro ratione voluntas,.
With an object-clause: jubeto, istos foras exire,: hae me litterae Dolabellae jubent ad pristinas cogitationes reverti,: Perdicca pueros equos jussit conscendere,: eos suum adventum exspectare jussit, so with pass.: deos iratos Tarentinis relinqui jussit,.—
With ut or ne: jubet sententiam ut dicat suam,: jubere ut haec quoque referret, etc.,; ; ; ; : jussitque ut quae venissent naves Euboeam peterent,; .— Esp. of decrees of the people: senatus decrevit populusque jussit, ut, etc.,; ; ; (cf. II. B. infra): quod ne fieret, consules jusserunt,. —
With subj. alone (ante-class. and postAug., Madv. Gr. § 390): jube, mihi denuo respondeat,; ; ; cf. esp. Weissenb.; 28, 36, 2: rescribat multa jubeto,; : 11, 588 al.—
With dat. pers.: qui scribae ... deos iratos Tarentinis relinqui jussit,: Hercules sacrorum custodibus jussit, ne mulierem interesse permitterent,: quibus jusserat, ut instantibus resisterent,: Britannico jussit, exsurgeret,: suis rex cultu feminarum abstinere jussit,.—(ε) With acc. pers. vel rei: jube famulos, rem divinam mihi apparent,: litterae non quae te aliquid juberent, sed, etc.,: sed tu jussisses Eurysthea,: neque jubere caedem fratris palam audebat,: Nero jussit scelera,.—(ζ) With acc. rei and dat. pers.: tributum iis Drusus jusserat modicum,imposed,; cf. II. B. 2. infra: pacem jubebo Omnibus,.—(η) Pass.: quod jussi sunt faciunt,: consules jubentur scribere exercitum,: opto ut ea potissimum jubear, quae, etc.,: Germanos non juberi, non regi,: jussi sunt aegri deferri,; cf.: locus lautiaque legatis praeberi jussa,.—
In partic.
To wish, desire, entreat, bid: jubeto habere bonum animum,: sperare nos amici jubent,: valde jubeo gaudere te, : Caesar te sine cura esse jussit,: Dionysium jube salvere,salute him for me,. —So ellipt.: jubeo Chremetem,.—
In polit. lang.
To order, decree, ratify, approve the introduction of a proposed law: quae scisceret plebs aut quae populus juberet,; : legem populus Romanus jussit de civitate tribuenda,: dicere apud populum de legibus jubendis aut vetandis,.—Absol. with de: de omnibus his—populum jussisse,.—
To designate, appoint, assign: Tullum Hostilium regem populus jussit, Weissenb.: id modo excepere ne postea eosdem tribunos juberent,: quem vos imperatorem jussistis,: postquam ei provinciam Numidiam populus jussit,allotted,.—
Hence the formula, Velitis, jubeatis, with which the magistrates called upon the people to confirm any thing proposed to them: rogationem promulgavit: vellent, juberent Philippo regi bellum indici,.—
Med. t. t., to prescribe, order: quod jussi ei dari bibere, date,; : aegrotus, qui jussus sit vinum sumere,.—
Transf.: qui modo, si volucres habuissem regna jubentes, In populo potui maximus esse meo,.

la:verb:iuro.gloss: to confirm formally, to pronounce enforceably, to swear, to vow, to take an oath
senses: to confirm formally, to pronounce enforceably, to swear, to vow, to take an oath
la:verb:iuro.html:
jūro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.
, and jūror, ātus, 1, v. dep.
2. jus
, to swear, to take an oath.
In gen., absol.: cui si aram tenens juraret, crederet nemo,: cum ille mihi nihil, nisi ut jurarem, permitteret,: cum enim faciles sint nonnulli hominum ad jurandum,: posteaquam juratum est, denegatur actio,: ex animi tui sententia jurāris,.— With inf., ; ; .—With nom. and inf., poet., .—With acc. and inf.: jurat, se eum non deserturum,: se non reversurum,: jurarem ... me et ardere studio veri reperiendi,: nisi victores se redituros jurant,: Boeotum in crasso jurares aëre natum,: falsum,to swear falsely,: vere,to swear truly,: jurarem per Jovem,by Jupiter,: per supremi regis regnum,; : per solis radios,; .—Also with simple acc. of the being or object sworn by (mostly poet.): Terram, Mare, Sidera,; : quomodo tibi placebit Jovem lapidem jurare, cum scias?: quaevis tibi numina,: Samothracum aras,.—Hence also pass.: dis juranda palus,the Styx, by which the gods swear,; cf.: Stygias juravimus undas,: Junonis numina,: caput,.— Rarely with acc. of the fact sworn to: morbum,i. e. to swear to the fact of sickness,; cf.: jurata pacta,: ex mei animi sententia,with sincerity, without reservation,; so, ex nostri animi sententia,; cf. ; : alicui aliquid,

to vow or promise to one, : sacramenta deis,: alicui jurare,to swear allegiance to,: in verba, to swear with certain words, i. e. to take a prescribed form of oath: Petreius in haec verba jurat,: cur in certa verba jurent,: milites in verba P. Scipionis jurarunt,; ; : in haec verba jures postulo,in this form of words,: in verba magistri,to echo his sentiments,: in verba ejus,: in verba Vitellii,: idem deinceps omnis exercitus in se quisque jurat, i. e. each soldier took the oath separately; whereas the usual practice was that one man uttered the entire oath, and the others only added, idem in me,: in litem,to make oath respecting the matter in dispute, to appraise under oath,; ; : in nomen alicujus,to swear allegiance to one,: in legem,to swear to observe a law,: verissimum pulcherrimumque jusjurandum,to take an oath,: sacramenta,; cf.: sceleri jurato nefando sacramenta,.—With de and abl.: de sua persona,in one's own behalf,: de calumnia,to clear one's self of calumny under oath,; .— Pass. impers.: scis, tibi ubique jurari,: ne in acta sua juraretur, Suet .—

Dep. form, ; cf. : judici demonstrandum est, quid juratus sit, quid sequi debeat,: ex lege, in quam jurati sitis,: juratus se eum sua manu interempturum,.—
In partic., to conspire (cf. conjuro); with inf.: jurarunt inter se barbaros necare, Cato ap. : in me jurarunt somnus, ventusque, fidesque,: in facinus,.—Hence, jūrātus, a, um, P. a.
Pass.
Called upon or taken to witness in an oath: numina,.—
Under an oath, bound by an oath: Regulus juratus missus est ad senatum, ut, etc.,: quamvis jurato metuam tibi credere testi,.—
Act., having sworn, that has sworn: nam injurato scio plus credet mihi quam jurato tibi,; : haec, quae juratus in maxima contione dixi,: in eadem arma,.—Sup.: juratissimi auctores, the most trustworthy, praef. § 22. —Adv.: jūrātō, with an oath, under oath (post-class.): promittere,.

la:verb:iudico.gloss: to examine judicially, judge, pass judgement, decide; condemn
senses: to examine judicially, judge, pass judgement, decide; condemn
to judge; proclaim; determine, conclude; adjudge
la:verb:iudico.html:
jūdĭco, āvi, ātum, 1 (judicassit for judicaverit, ), v. a.
judex
,
to examine judicially, to judge, be a judge, pass judgment, decide (syn.: judicium facio, reddo; class.).
Lit.: si recte et ordine judicaris,: cum magistratus judicassit,: ordo alius ad res judicandas postulatur,: aliquid contra aliquem,: judicare, deberi viro dotem,: homo in rebus judicandis spectatus et cognitus,: judicantem vidimus Aeacum,: ad judicandum evocari,: ne aut spoliaret fama probatum virum, si contra judicavisset,: de bene meritis civibus potestas judicandi,: res,; : ex aequo et bono,: mihi tris hodie litis judicandas dicito,.—With kindred acc.: inclytum judicium, Poët. ap. . —Esp.,
To condemn = damnare; quo jam diu sum judicatus,: judicati atque addicti,; : judicatum pecuniae,: quoad vel capitis vel pecuniae judicasset privato,: quique judicati pecuniae in vinculis essent,: judicare aliquem pecuniae,to fine,: alicui perduellionem judicare,.—
Transf. beyond the legal sphere.
To judge, judge of a thing: aliquid oculorum fallacissimo sensu,: quod egomet multis argumentis jam antea judicāram,: sic statuo et judico, neminem, etc.,.—
To declare, proclaim a person to be any thing: judicetur non verbo sed re, non modo non consul, sed etiam, hostis Antonius,: Deiotarum unum fidelem populo Romano,: cujus rei exemplum pulcherrimum judicarem,.—
To determine, resolve, conclude: de itinere ipsos brevi tempore judicaturos,.—
To adjudge, make over to a person: nam ego ad Menaechmum nunc eo, cui jam diu Sum judicatus (al. quo),: judicata pecunia,.—Hence, jūdĭ-cātus, a, um, P. a., decided, determined: mihi judicatum est deponere illam personam,I am determined,: res judicata,a decided matter taken as a precedent for other cases,; : infirmatio rerum judicatarum,.—Also, sentenced, condemned: judicatum duci,. —Hence, subst.: jūdĭcātum, i, n., a matter judged or decided; a decision, judgment, precedent, authority: judicatum est id, de quo sententia lata est, aut decretum interpositum,: judicatum est, de quo ante jam sententia alicujus ... constitutum est,; : quamvis postea judicatum fiat, tamen actio data non intercidit,.—
An award, a fine: solvere,; .—Adv.: jūdĭcātō, deliberately (post-class.), .

jūdĭcātus, ūs, m.
judico

la:noun:iudicium.html:
jūdĭcĭum, ii, n.
judex
,
a judgment, i. e. a judicial investigation, trial; a judicial sentence (class.).
Lit.: omnia judicia aut distrahendarum controversiarum aut puniendorum maleficiorum causā reperta sunt,: dignitatis meae,concerning,: praetor judicium prius de probro, quam de re fieri maluit,: de alicujus meritis judicia facere,: de mea fide,: de se,: inter sicarios,for assassination,: adducere causam aliquam in judicium,: judicio aliquid defendere,: agere,to settle a dispute,: ferre, to give his vote; of a judge (different from sententiam ferre, to pass sentence), Orell.: exercere,: vocare aliquem in judicium,to summon before court,: judicio quempiam arcessere,to sue,: sistere in judicium,to set before the court,: dare, to allow, grant a trial, of the prætor who proposes the judges: in Lurconis libertum judicium ex edicto dedit,: judicium accipere, suscipere,to undertake a legal trial,; : pati,to submit to,: damnatus inani judicio Marius,. —
Transf.
A court of justice: at ille in judicium venit,: judicium clauserat militibus armatis,. —
Beyond the legal sphere, a judgment, decision, opinion with regard to any thing: meum semper judicium fuit, omnia nostros invenisse per se sapientius quam, etc.,: decima legio per tribunos militum ei gratias egit, quod de se optimum judicium fecisset,: judicium facere, quanti quisque sibi faciendus esset,to judge, decide,: meo judicio,in my judgment, according to my opinion,; : ex alicujus judicio,: de quo homine vos tanta et tam praeclara judicia fecistis, i. e. by conferring honors on him, .—
The power of judging, judgment, discernment: studio optimo, judicio minus firmo praeditus,; : intellegens,: subtile,: si quid mei judicii est,if I can judge of it,: videor id judicio facere,i. e. with discretion, good judgment,; so ; dub.: adhibere,: acri judicio perpendere aliquid,.—
Judicial harangues, speeches in court: illa mala judicia,.

sup. form from jugis; v. jungo
,

Adv.
Lit., of place.
Of several objects, near together, in close proximity: theatra duo juxta fecit amplissima e ligno,.—
In gen., near at hand, near, near by, hard by, close to, by the side of: legio, quae juxta constiterat,: ut sellam juxta poneret,: furiarum maxima juxta Accubat,: forte fuit juxta tumulus,: procul vel juxta sitas vires circumspectabat,: talem perlatum Pompeio juxta res gerenti Mithridatico bello, : abjecto clam juxta pugione,: thermisque juxta celeriter constructis,.— Rarely with verbs of motion: accedere juxta,.—
Transf., in like manner, equally, alike (syn.: aeque, pariter).
Absol.: eorum ego vitam mortemque juxta aestimo,: aestatem et hiemem juxta pati,: ceteri juxta insontes,: qui Argenta habent, aliaque castella juxta ignobilia,: juxta periculosum seu ficta seu vera promeret,: solo caeloque juxta gravi,.—
With dat.: Fabius omittendam rem parvam ac juxta magnis difficilem censebat,.—
With ac, atque, et, quam, cum, in the sense of as, than (cf.: aeque ac, pariter ac, etc.): juxta tecum aeque scio,: juxta eam curo cum mea, (so always in Plaut.; v. Prep., with acc., very near, close to, near to, hard by (not ante-class.).

According to: juxta praeceptum,; ; : juxta morem,: juxta hoc videtur et divus Hadrianus rescripsisse in haec verba,: juxta inclytum oratorem,.
